73597-the-three-strings.title: Three Strings
73597-the-three-strings.creator: Natalie Sumner Lincoln
73597-the-three-strings.description: A book by Natalie Sumner Lincoln. EVELYN PRESTON ran lightly up the steps of her home and inserting her latch-key in the vestibule door, pushed it open just as the taxi-driver, following more slowly with many an upward glance at the blind-closed windows, reached her side.

arxiv-1501-00820.title: Software Safety Demonstration and Indemnification
arxiv-1501-00820.creator: Odell Hegna
arxiv-1501-00820.description: Abstract Computers may control safety-critical operations in machines having embedded software. This memoir proposes a regimen to verify such algorithms at prescribed levels of statistical confidence. The United States Department of Defense standard for system safety engineering ( MIL-STD-882E ) defines development procedures for safety-critical systems.

arxiv-2109-10356.title: Formation and evolution of young massive clusters in galaxy mergers: the SMUGGLE view 2022 Formation and evolution of young massive clusters in galaxy mergers: the SMUGGLE view – B.0.2
arxiv-2109-10356.creator: Hui Li , Mark Vogelsberger , Greg L. Bryan , Federico Marinacci , Laura V. Sales , Paul Torrey
arxiv-2109-10356.description: Abstract Galaxy mergers are known to host abundant young massive cluster (YMC) populations, whose formation mechanism is still not well-understood. Here, we present a high-resolution galaxy merger simulation with explicit star formation and stellar feedback prescriptions to investigate how mergers affect the properties of the interstellar medium and YMCs.

arxiv-2201-05490.title: An Almost Globally Stable Adaptive Phase-Locked Loop for Synchronization of a Grid-Connected Voltage Source Converter
arxiv-2201-05490.creator: Daniele Zonetti, Alexey Bobtsov, Romeo Ortega, Nikolay Nikolaev, Oriol Gomis-Bellmunt
arxiv-2201-05490.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Daniele Zonetti, Alexey Bobtsov, Romeo Ortega, Nikolay Nikolaev, Oriol Gomis-Bellmunt. In this paper we are interested in the problem of adaptive synchronization of a voltage source converter with a possibly weak grid with unknown angle and frequency, but knowledge of its parameters. To guarantee a suitable synchronization with the angle of the three-phase grid voltage we design an adaptive observer for such a signal requiring measurements only at the point of common coupling.

arxiv-2204-06533.title: Modified theories of Gravity: Why, How and What?
arxiv-2204-06533.creator: S. Shankaranarayanan, Joseph P Johnson
arxiv-2204-06533.description: Abstract General Relativity (GR) was proven via the direct detection of gravitational waves from the mergers of the binary black holes and binary neutron stars by the Advanced LIGO and Advanced Virgo detectors. These detections confirmed the prediction of GR and provided the first direct evidence of the existence of stellar-mass black holes (BHs).

arxiv-2309-04834.title: Particle-in-cell simulations of pulsar magnetospheres: transition between electrosphere and force-free regimes
arxiv-2309-04834.creator: F. Cruz, T. Grismayer, A. Y. Chen, A. Spitkovsky, R. A. Fonseca, L. O. Silva
arxiv-2309-04834.description: Abstract Aims. Global particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations of pulsar magnetospheres are performed with a volume, surface and pair production-based plasma injection schemes to systematically investigate the transition between electrosphere and force-free pulsar magnetospheric regimes. Methods. A new extension of the PIC code OSIRIS to model pulsar magnetospheres using a two-dimensional axisymmetric spherical grid is presented.

arxiv-2312-17188.title: Development of a new CEDAR for kaon identification at the NA62 experiment at CERN
arxiv-2312-17188.creator: The NA62 collaboration
arxiv-2312-17188.description: Abstract The NA62 experiment at CERN utilises a differential Cherenkov counter with achromatic ring focus (CEDAR) for tagging kaons within an unseparated monochromatic beam of charged hadrons. The CEDAR-H detector was developed to minimise the amount of material in the path of the beam by using hydrogen gas as the radiator medium.

arxiv-2402-10574.title: Nowcasting with Mixed Frequency Data Using Gaussian Processes
arxiv-2402-10574.description: Abstract Niko HAUZENBERGER University of Strathclyde, United Kingdom Massimiliano MARCELLINO Bocconi University, IGIER, Baffi, Bidsa, CEPR, Italy Michael PFARRHOFER WU Vienna, Austria Anna STELZER Oesterreichische Nationalbank, Austria We develop Bayesian machine learning methods for mixed data sampling (MIDAS) regressions. This involves handling frequency mismatches and specifying functional relationships between many predictors and the dependent variable.

arxiv-2403-14188.title: Quantum-activated neural reservoirs on-chip open up large hardware security models for resilient authentication
arxiv-2403-14188.creator: Zhao He 1 †, Maxim S. Elizarov 1 †, Ning Li 1, Fei Xiang 1, and Andrea Fratalocchi 1
arxiv-2403-14188.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Zhao He 1 †, Maxim S. Elizarov 1 †, Ning Li 1, Fei Xiang 1, and Andrea Fratalocchi 1. Quantum artificial intelligence is a frontier of artificial intelligence research, pioneering quantum AI-powered circuits to address problems beyond the reach of deep learning with classical architectures.

arxiv-2410-09054.title: Circuits and Systems for Embodied AI: Exploring uJ Multi-Modal Perception for Nano-UAVs on the Kraken Shield
arxiv-2410-09054.creator: Viviane Potocnik 2 , Alfio Di Mauro 2 , Lorenzo Lamberti 3 , Victor Kartsch 2 , Moritz Scherer 2 , Francesco Conti 3 , Luca Benini 2 3
arxiv-2410-09054.description: Abstract Embodied artificial intelligence (AI) requires pushing complex multi-modal models to the extreme edge for time-constrained tasks such as autonomous navigation of robots and vehicles. On small form-factor devices, e.g., nano-sized unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), such challenges are exacerbated by stringent constraints on energy efficiency and weight.

arxiv-2410-21997.title: XUV yield optimization of two-color high-order harmonic generation in gases
arxiv-2410-21997.creator: Ann-Kathrin Raab, Melvin Redon, Sylvianne Roscam Abbing, Yuman Fang, Chen Guo, Peter Smorenburg, Johan Mauritsson, Anne-Lise Viotti, Anne L’Huillier, Cord L. Arnold
arxiv-2410-21997.description: Abstract We perform an experimental two-color high-order harmonic generation study in argon with the fundamental of an ytterbium ultrashort pulse laser and its second harmonic. The intensity of the second harmonic and its phase relative to the fundamental are varied, in a large range compared to earlier works, while keeping the total intensity constant.

arxiv-2510-07615.title: XRISM /Resolve observations of Hercules X-1: vertical structure and kinematics of the disk wind Facilities: XRISM , XMM-Newton , NuSTAR , Chandra Veusz, SPEX ( J. S. Kaastra et al. 1996 ) , XSPEC ( K. A. Arnaud 1996 )
arxiv-2510-07615.creator: Peter Kosec, Laura Brenneman, Erin Kara, Teruaki Enoto, Takuto Narita, Koh Sakamoto, Rüdiger Staubert, Francesco Barra, Andrew Fabian, Jon M. Miller, Ciro Pinto, Daniele Rogantini, Dominic Walton, Yutaro Nagai
arxiv-2510-07615.description: Abstract X-ray binary accretion disk winds can carry away a significant fraction of the originally infalling matter and hence strongly affect the accretion flow and the long-term evolution of the binary system. However, accurate measurements of their mass outflow rates are challenging due to uncertainties in our understanding of the 3D wind structure.

arxiv-2601-16182.title: Dynamic Pattern Matching with Wildcards
arxiv-2601-16182.creator: Arshia Ataee Naeini, Amir-Parsa Mobed, Masoud Seddighin, Saeed Seddighin
arxiv-2601-16182.description: Abstract We study the fully dynamic pattern matching problem where the pattern may contain up to k k wildcard symbols, each matching any symbol of the alphabet. Both the text and the pattern are subject to updates (insert, delete, change).

pmc-10738988.title: FEASIBILITY OF AN AUTOMATED SELF-ADMINISTERED 24 HOUR (ASA-24) DIETARY ASSESSMENT TOOL IN OLDER ADULTS
pmc-10738988.creator: Hillary Spangler, Tiffany Driesse, Michael Fowler, David Lynch, Danae Gross, Xiaohui Liang, John Batsis
pmc-10738988.description: BackgroundCertain dietary patterns impact trajectories of healthy aging. However, dietary assessment tools can be challenging to use. With the increased technology use in older adults, we aimed to explore the feasibility of completing an online, Automated Self-Administered 24-hour (ASA-24) dietary assessment tool.

pmc-11432663.title: Synergistic Effect between the APOE ε4 Allele with Genetic Variants of GSK3B and MAPT: Differential Profile between Refractory Epilepsy and Alzheimer Disease
pmc-11432663.creator: Danira Toral-Rios, Pavel Pichardo-Rojas, Elizabeth Ruiz-Sánchez, Óscar Rosas-Carrasco, Rosa Carvajal-García, Dey Carol Gálvez-Coutiño, Nancy Lucero Martínez-Rodríguez, Ana Daniela Rubio-Chávez, Myr Alcántara-Flores, Arely López-Ramírez, Alma Rosa Martínez-Rosas, Ángel Alberto Ruiz-Chow, Mario Alonso
pmc-11432663.description: Temporal Lobe Epilepsy (TLE) is a chronic neurological disorder characterized by recurrent focal seizures originating in the temporal lobe. Despite the variety of antiseizure drugs currently available to treat TLE, about 30% of cases continue to have seizures. The etiology of TLE is complex and multifactorial.

pmc-11606842.title: Gymnema lactiferum: A Review of Its Traditional Applications, Phytochemical Constituents, and Biological Properties
pmc-11606842.creator: D. M. K. P. Weerasinghe, L. Brough, D. W. Everett, A. Rashidinejad
pmc-11606842.description: Humanity has a longstanding reliance on natural plants for medicinal purposes, and Gymnema lactiferum (G. lactiferum) has emerged as a medicinal plant with deep‐rooted traditional usage. Throughout history, this plant has been an integral part of traditional medical systems, demonstrating diverse therapeutic effects.

pmc-11663388.title: Deep Learning-Based Automatic Segmentation Combined with Radiomics to Predict Post-TACE Liver Failure in HCC Patients
pmc-11663388.creator: Shuai Li, Kaicai Liu, Chang Rong, Xiaoming Zheng, Bo Cao, Wei Guo, Xingwang Wu
pmc-11663388.description: ObjectiveTo develop and validate a deep learning-based automatic segmentation model and combine with radiomics to predict post-TACE liver failure (PTLF) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients.MethodsThis was a retrospective study enrolled 210 TACE-trated HCC patients. Automatic segmentation model based on nnU-Net neural network was developed to segment medical images and assessed by the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC).

pmc-13265700.title: Experience-dependent cortical plasticity in response to formal schooling: Effects on networks for reading and mathematics
pmc-13265700.creator: Floor Vandecruys, Maaike Vandermosten, Bert De Smedt
pmc-13265700.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Between ages 5–10, children undergo substantial structural brain development. These changes coincide with the transition from preschool to primary school. The extent to which this school transition drives the observed structural brain changes remains unclear. We used a school cut-off design to disentangle the effects of formal schooling and age-related maturation on children’s brain development by comparing children who attended formal education in primary school and children of similar age but who remained in preschool.

pmc-13346605.title: The development of FEDUPP: feeding experimentation device users processing package to assess learning and cognitive flexibility
pmc-13346605.creator: Mingyang Yao, Avraham M. Libster, Shane Desfor, Freiya Malhotra, Nathalia Castorena, Patricia Montilla-Perez, Francesca Telese
pmc-13346605.description: Cognitive flexibility, the ability to adapt behavior in response to changing contingencies, is a key component of adaptive decision-making and is impaired in multiple neuropsychiatric disorders. Traditional rodent assays of cognitive flexibility are conducted in experimenter-controlled sessions in restrictive environments, limiting ecological validity and temporal resolution.

pmc-13462800.title: Indigenous excellence: confronting racism and complicity in peer review
pmc-13462800.creator: Raglan Maddox, Sarah Funnell, Michelle Kennedy, Janet Smylie
pmc-13462800.description: Racism in peer review is a common, structurally embedded, and systemic problem. However, it is often framed as isolated acts of individual-level bias. Racism in peer review manifests across interconnected societal, system, and process levels, shaping who participates in knowledge production, what is deemed credible evidence, and whose work is published.

uslaw-usc-t36-s152506.description: United States Code, Title 36 (Patriotic And National Observances, Ceremonies, And Organizations); Part B (Organizations); Chapter 1525 (National Safety Council). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel.
